references.text: The context for this verse: Jesus heals a boy with an unclean spirit, which leads everyone to be amazed at the greatness of God.
The people were amazed (ἐξεπλήσσοντο) by Jesus' teaching; the same Greek verb is used here as in Luke 9:43.
After a healing, all were seized with wonder and praised God—a similar reaction to that in Luke 9:43 where everyone was astonished at the greatness of God.
Matthew's parallel account where Jesus predicts his suffering and death right after healing the boy, corresponding to the second part of Luke 9:43 where Jesus speaks to his disciples.
In Mark's parallel account, the crowd was greatly amazed when they saw Jesus—a similar reaction of wonder.
Mark's parallel where Jesus teaches the disciples about his impending suffering and death, corresponding to Jesus' words to the disciples in the second half of Luke 9:43.
Matthew's parallel account of the healing of the boy where the crowd witnesses Jesus' power, which lies behind the people's amazement in Luke 9:43.

The direct continuation where Jesus tells the disciples that the Son of Man will be handed over into human hands—the content of what Jesus said to the disciples according to the last part of verse 43.
The people praised God after Jesus raised the widow's son in Nain—a similar reaction to the greatness of God as in Luke 9:43.
The crowd rejoiced over all the wonderful deeds Jesus did—parallel to everyone being amazed at everything he did (πᾶσιν οἷς ἐποίει).
Peter uses the word μεγαλειότητι (greatness/majesty) to describe Christ's greatness which he witnessed firsthand—the same rare word used in Luke 9:43 regarding God's greatness.
